full_judgment: 5. Mr. M.A. Wahab the learned Deputy Attorney General appeared on behalf of the State. He supported the order passed by the learned Sessions Judge and submits that no illegality has been committed by the learned Sessions Judge in extending the time for investigation. According to him the Sessions Judge had jurisdiction to extend time and there was no limitation as to extension of time by him. It is correct that investigation was not completed within 30 days from the date of lodging the F.T.R. nor the same was completed within - the extended period of 30 days granted by the Magistrate whereupon the investigating officer prayed before the Sessions Judge for further extension of time for investigation as per pro-vision of section 167(6) Cr.P.C. The learned Sessions Judge extended time on an application filed by the Investigating Officer. The amended section 167 (6) Cr.P.C. is as follows: "Where further investigation into an offence is stopped on the expiry either of the specified time or of the extended time under sub-section (5), the Sessions Judge may, if he is satisfied. on an application made to him or otherwise, that further investigation into the offence ought to be made, direct further investigation to be made, into the offence subject to such directions with regard to bail and other matters as he may specify."
